outcome.outcome: Releasing a capable model stops meaning releasing its worst uses along with it.
outcome.rationale: Their two capabilities target robustness and decentralised control, both aimed at decoupling capability from misusability.

ai_types.rationale: Jailbreak resistance is a research problem with measurable progress; what binds is whether safeguards are adopted uniformly across providers.
Adversarial robustness training and automated red-teaming are working techniques already in production.

measurability.rationale: Jailbreak success rates on benchmark suites are measurable, but misuse actually averted is unobserved, so the gap itself is measured only through adjacent indicators.

outcome.outcome: You can check a claim about an AI system against its internals, rather than infer it from behaviour on tests the system may recognise.
outcome.rationale: Their capability list leads with automated interpretability and guaranteed-safe architectures, both aimed at making assurance verifiable.

ai_types.rationale: Automating interpretability means using models to explain models, which is a reasoning task over learned representations.
Hardware governance appears in their own capability list and is a control-and-allocation mechanism, not a technique.

measurability.rationale: Evaluations and interpretability probes exist and are run, but there is no agreement in the field that any of them would settle whether a system is safe. This is a verifier problem rather than a measurement problem.

outcome.outcome: An AI system handles a domain it was not trained on without someone rebuilding the scaffolding around it.
outcome.rationale: Their description contrasts narrow current capability with human cognition and names general intelligence as the target.

ai_types.rationale: This gap is definitionally about the reasoning capability itself; all five listed capabilities are training or architecture approaches to it.

measurability.rationale: Reasoning benchmarks exist and are run constantly, but the field openly disputes whether benchmark performance measures general reasoning or contamination and pattern coverage. A measurement can always be taken; what it shows is what is argued about.

outcome.outcome: We get a second example of complex evolved computation to generalise from. At present biology is the only one.
outcome.rationale: Their description states the problem as biology being the sole example; the unlock is a second one.

ai_types.rationale: The listed capability is virtual life on GPUs, which is large-scale simulation of evolving systems; nothing at the required open-endedness has been demonstrated.

measurability.rationale: Complexity and open-endedness metrics exist and can be computed on any simulation, but there is no agreement that any of them distinguishes genuine evolved complexity from an artifact of the fitness landscape.

outcome.outcome: Whole classes of vulnerability stop being possible, rather than being found and patched one at a time.
outcome.rationale: Their description names formal methods and verification as the route, and the unlock is elimination rather than detection.

ai_types.rationale: Proof synthesis paired with a checker is the archetypal verifiable task, and models are already competitive on it at small scale.

measurability.rationale: Proportion of a critical codebase carrying machine-checked proofs, and vulnerability counts in verified versus unverified components, are directly countable.

outcome.outcome: Formal verification stops costing more than the proof it verifies, and machine-assisted proof turns routine at research level.
outcome.rationale: Their capability is reinforcement learning from theorem-prover feedback, aimed at making proof search practical.

ai_types.rationale: A theorem prover is a perfect verifier, which is exactly the condition under which AI progress has been fastest, and competition-level results are already in hand.

measurability.rationale: A proof either checks in a formal system or it does not, and benchmark theorem sets with formalisation rates already exist.

outcome.outcome: Energy stops setting the ceiling on how much inference and simulation science can afford to run. Orders of magnitude more compute per joule.
outcome.rationale: Their description names scalability and sustainability as the losses, and energy is the shared constraint across all eleven capabilities.

ai_types.rationale: Architecture and chip design search is where AI acts on this; their own list opens with AI-based design of AI chips.
Neuromorphic, reversible and thermodynamic computing all require fabricating device physics that no production process supports.

measurability.rationale: Joules per operation at a stated workload is a direct and universally reported figure.

outcome.outcome: Compute keeps getting cheaper per operation after silicon channel physics gives out.
outcome.rationale: Their description is unusually specific that the limits are fundamental and material, not engineering.

ai_types.rationale: Identifying and optimising 2D semiconductor stacks is a materials search problem with a well-specified objective.
Process development for a new channel material is an iterative fabricate-and-measure loop, which is what closed-loop experimentation automates.

measurability.rationale: Gate length, carrier mobility and on-off ratio at manufacturable yield are direct device metrics.

notes: Real taxonomy strain: semiconductor process and device-physics development has no clean home, sitting between 'Design and optimization search' and 'Physical build and manipulation'. Affects both silicon gaps; both marked guess on the primary. Three tier-3 calls here, all on AI-about-AI questions where the field cannot agree what would count as evidence — the same verifier problem as quantum gravity, in a different domain.
